findings.reason: Same defect and same code block as the ground-truth bug: exclusion syntax read loosely so a find that still walks the archive counts as excluding it. Verified by running.

findings.summary: Searcher skip regex `-[A-Za-z]*[egtTIE]` marks the next word as an option value for flags that take none (grep -E, rg -I), so `grep -e foo -E archive/old.md` is allowed
findings.reason: Confirmed from the diff: -E/-I are in the skip class but take no value, so a real archive operand is skipped. A real bypass not in the known-bug list.

findings.summary: MENTIONS_ARCHIVE matches any path containing an `archive` segment, so `rg -g '!src/archive/**'` and Grep glob `!src/archive/**` count as excluding the root archive
findings.reason: Exclusion flag read loosely so a search that still walks the root archive counts as excluding it — the defect the ground-truth bug describes, in the same exclusion-parsing code.

findings.summary: grep `--exclude=archive` (a file-name glob) is in EXCLUDE_LONG, so `grep -r --exclude=archive foo .` is allowed though grep recurses into archive/
findings.reason: Exactly the `grep --exclude=archive (file pattern)` case listed in the ground truth.

findings.summary: First negative archive glob ends the check; a later positive glob re-includes the archive: `rg foo -g '!archive' -g 'archive/**'` allowed

findings.summary: Move-in exception lets `mv docs/a.md archive/old.md` / git mv overwrite an existing archived file

fixed.reason: No change to how the shell's working directory is tracked across commands: nothing in the diff touches subshell cd, failed cd, cd -, pushd/popd, env -C or sudo -D. Only git's own -C/--work-tree/--git-dir handling inside commandTouches was adjusted, which is a different path.

shell.mjs changes only export GIT_VALUE_OPTS; parseCommands and commandTouches gain no handling for find -exec, fish -c, watch, xargs -a, env -S, python -c or node -e. Those nested commands are still not inspected.

Glued pattern-file values (grep -farchive/old.md) are now treated as file reads and tested. But $'…' quoting, [[:alpha:]]rchive classes, ar(c|x)hive, ~+/archive and dd if=archive/… are untouched; globRegex only gained a try/catch for classes the RegExp constructor rejects.

excludesArchive was rewritten per tool: grep --exclude no longer counts (only --exclude-dir), a positive rg glob matching the archive voids !archive, findPrunes returns false with -delete/-depth and requires the prune to lead the expression, tar's value regex rejects /archive, and zip -x needs 'archive/*'. All five listed cases are in DENIED and the correct forms in ALLOWED.

The .ignore check now runs per repository reached (repos.every with each root's own .ignore/.rgignore), and positive globs like -g '*' or 'archive/**' override it, so rg -g '*' foo and rg foo <other-repo> are now denied. But -L/--follow is not in IGNORE_OFF and re-includes (!archive) in .rgignore are not read, so those routes still count as excluding.

walkRoots makes revision operands walk the tree from the top, so git grep foo HEAD, git ls-tree -r HEAD and git archive HEAD are denied (tested). But git log -p, git show <commit>, cat-file --batch, clone . <dir> and the rest are not handled; the ADR change explicitly documents git log -p / git show as still open.

The move-in branch now refuses a glob destination and checks whether the destination file exists, or, for a directory destination, whether an entry matching each source's basename (glob-aware) already exists there. The check does not depend on -f, so mv -f and git mv -f are covered; mv docs/a.md archive/old.md and mv docs/*.md archive/ are in DENIED.
The walker table in walk() is not changed; tar -rf, bsdtar, pax -w, 7z, ditto, scp -r and diff -r remain unlisted and still copy the archive unchecked.

None of the listed false refusals (npm run archive, git checkout -b archive, git log --grep=archive, ls -d */, du -sh *, Glob '*', git add archive/old.md) is addressed; the path loop still treats every non-flag word as a path and Glob still resolves the bare pattern. Only searcher option values (rg -l archive docs) are newly skipped, which is a different case.

hook.mjs is not touched; the archive block still has no deny-on-error wrapper, so any exception (e.g. a non-string cwd) still reaches the fail-open catch. The try/catch added in globRegex guards only one internal RegExp failure.
